subtitle: Learn bookkeeping, GST and audit evidence on a simulated New Zealand business

chapters.title: What ByteBook is, and what this handbook is for
chapters.summary: A bookkeeping program that keeps your books on your own computer, and a way to learn on a business that cannot be hurt.

chapters.title: Set up a training business
chapters.summary: Install ByteBook, answer four questions, and give yourself a role you can hand over.

chapters.title: The twelve businesses you can practise on
chapters.summary: Each simulation sets up a different New Zealand business, trades it, banks it and files it — then checks the books from the raw rows.

chapters.title: Invoices: selling on paper and in the books
chapters.summary: Raise an invoice, decide when it reaches the ledger, and see why a draft is not yet revenue.

chapters.title: Payments, and the money you are owed
chapters.summary: Record the money as it arrives, keep the aged debtors list honest, and know what a credit balance means.

chapters.title: Bills, expenses and the documents behind them
chapters.summary: Record what the business owes and spends, and keep the piece of paper that proves it was a business cost.

chapters.title: The bank statement, line by line
chapters.summary: Import a CSV, code each line, reconcile against the statement, and understand why this screen catches the most mistakes.

chapters.title: GST: the return built from your own transactions
chapters.summary: Work out a GST return from the ledger, check the boxes against your transactions, and save a snapshot before you file.

chapters.title: Reports: what each one answers
chapters.summary: Six reports, one question each — and how to check that a report is telling you the truth.

chapters.title: Closing a month and a year
chapters.summary: The routine that turns a month of coding into a set of books somebody else can rely on.

chapters.title: Nothing is deleted: voiding, not editing
chapters.summary: Why the correction is more valuable than the tidy-up, and how a void keeps both the mistake and the fix in the record.

chapters.title: The audit trail and the chain
chapters.summary: Every entry carries a fingerprint that includes the one before it. Change an old number and the chain says so.

chapters.title: The sixteen assurance procedures
chapters.summary: An audit programme you can run on the real rows — what each procedure asks, and what its exceptions mean.

chapters.title: Sealed packs and working papers
chapters.summary: Close a period so it cannot change quietly, hand over a file an auditor can follow, and know what stays outside the program.

chapters.title: Roles: who may do what
chapters.summary: Four roles, one rule about who can hand out access, and why the read-only login is the point of the feature.

chapters.title: How to read a standard reference
chapters.summary: What the letters and numbers mean, where each document comes from, and how to follow one to its source.

chapters.title: Accounting standards you will meet in these books
chapters.summary: The standards behind the numbers, the question each one answers, and the screen in ByteBook where it shows up.

chapters.title: Auditing standards you will meet in these procedures
chapters.summary: From objectives and evidence to the opinion — the ISAs (NZ) behind the sixteen procedures.

chapters.title: Screen by screen: which standards apply where
chapters.summary: One table that takes you from the thing you are looking at to the document that governs it.

chapters.title: How this handbook stays accurate
chapters.summary: Where every reference came from, how it is checked, and what to do when a standard changes.

chapters.title: Twelve training sessions
chapters.summary: One session per business, each with a task, the skills it builds, and a marking note.

chapters.title: Answers to the check-yourself questions
chapters.summary: Short answers, chapter by chapter, so a learner can mark their own work.

chapters.title: Glossary
chapters.summary: The words this handbook uses, in plain language.
